# One copy of a looped node is null-tested on every target a test can execute
# on: testdata/indexed_ref_null_test.txtar is the code. The second test moves
# which iteration the `if` leaves out, so a copy that was rendered is not and
# one that was not is.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

output {
    go {
        bubbletea
        fyne
        gtk4
    }
    kotlin {
        android
    }
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main node {
    var items = ["a", "b", "c"]
    var skip = "a"
    var log = ""
    vbox {
        button #change(text="skip b", @click { skip = "b" })
        for var it = items {
            if it != skip {
                button #only(text=it, @click { log = it })
                checkbox #tick(label=it, @change(on) { log = "{it} {on}" })
            }
        }
        text(value=log)
    }
}

func testOneCopyIsRendered(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.only[0] == null)
    t.assert(c.tick[0] == null)
    if c.only[1] != null {
        c.only[1].click()
    }
    t.assert(c.log == "b")
    t.assert(c.tick[2] != null)
}

func testAfterTheBranchChanges(t Test, c main) {
    c.change.click()
    t.assert(c.only[0] != null)
    t.assert(c.only[1] == null)
    t.assert(c.tick[1] == null)
    t.assert(c.tick[0] != null)
}

window {
    main
}
